previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, chronic systolic heart failure, and seizure disorder was admitted for epigastric abdominal pain and vomiting. Initial imaging showed gallbladder wall thickening concerning for cholecystitis, prompting treatment with antibiotics. A HIDA scan ruled out acute cholecystitis but revealed delayed tracer emptying, suggestive of sphincter of Oddi spasm. Symptoms improved with conservative management and anti-nausea medication. Elevated liver enzymes were noted but attributed to chronic changes; hepatitis workup was initiated. The patient remained afebrile, with resolution of symptoms, and was discharged home on unchanged medications with follow-up in gastroenterology.

A ___ year-old-man with history of ESRD on HD, DM I complicated

At time of admission to floor (after receiving Zofran in the ED 
and after undergoing hemodialysis for 4L fluid removal), his

baseline.

2. Hypoxia, increasing oxygen requirements.
He had a CXR in the ED that showed mild pulmonary edema; then he 
had 4L fluid removed at hemodialysis. On arrival to floor he had 
desats to low ___ on room-air; he was entirely asymptomatic 
during these episodes, with no dyspnea, cough, or respiratory 
distress. Lung exam did not show crackles. There was no pitting 
edema or JVD to suggest volume overload. He underwent CXR that 
showed question of LLL and RML infiltrate, and as he had a 
low-grade fever of 100.0, he was started empirically on 
levofloxacin for HAP. Overnight, he was weaned off of oxygen. He 
was afebrile. On the second hospital day, repeat CXR showed no 
evidence of pneumonia. His oxygen sats were mid to high ___ on 
RA and remained this way during ambulation. Levofloxacin was 
stopped. He had a chest CT that showed no pulmonary process. The 
cause for his transient hypoxemia after HD is still unclear; we 
think that it may be due to volume shift and hypoventilation 
immediately after HD. He has had good oxygen sats for over 48 
hours now on room air, with no cough or fever or other signs of 
infection.

We continued his home Lantus and Humolog insulin sliding scale. 
Blood sugars were well-controlled in the 150-160s.

We continued his outpatient BB, ___, and added aspirin.

We continued his outpatient Losartan and metoprolol.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ male with end-stage renal disease, on dialysis.
Abdominal pain and hypoxia.

COMPARISON:  CXR ___.

PORTABLE UPRIGHT CHEST:  Mild upper lung zone pulmonary vascular distribution
persists.  Interstitial markings appear more prominent compared with day
prior, suggesting a component of mild interstitial edema.  No definite focal
lung opacities are observed.  Trace bilateral pleural effusions may persist
compared to a day prior.  There is no pneumothorax.  Cardiomegaly appears
stable as do the mediastinal contours.  No pneumoperitoneum is identified
under the diaphragms.

IMPRESSION:  Cardiomegaly with mild upper lung zone re-distribution and a
suggestion of mild interstitial edema.

INDICATION:  ___ male with abdominal pain and distention.  Evaluate
for small-bowel obstruction.

COMPARISON:  Abdominal radiographs ___.

SUPINE ABDOMEN, SINGLE VIEW:  The bowel gas pattern is unremarkable and no
abnormally dilated loops of bowel are seen.  Stool and air are noted
throughout the colon with stool and air also seen in the rectum.  There is no
evidence for pneumoperitoneum on this single supine view.  The surrounding
osseous structures appear unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of obstruction.

INDICATION:  ___ man with abdominal distention, pain in the right
upper quadrant and nausea and vomiting for two days.  He has had hepatorenal
failure, on hemodialysis, and underwent recent liver biopsy.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained through the abdomen and
pelvis following administration of intravenous contrast material.  Multiplanar
reformatted images were generated.

CT ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:  At the lung bases, there is a small right
pleural effusion, and diffuse ground-glass opacities of both lungs suggesting
fluid overload or expiratory phase of imaging.  The heart is mildly enlarged.
There is no pericardial effusion.

In the abdomen, the liver again demonstrates a 1 cm focal hyperdense lesion in
segment VIII. This is unchanged from the most recent study of eleven days
prior, but was not visualized on ___ CT. The liver is otherwise
homogeneous without other focal lesions or ductal dilatation. There is a trace
amount of ascites surrounding the liver.

The gallbladder is unchanged in appearance from the exam of 11 days
prior.  It is not distended, and contains no stones. The pancreas, spleen,
adrenal glands, and duodenum are unremarkable.  The kidneys are atrophic, and
demonstrates delayed contrast enhancement consistent with renal failure.  The
stomach is fluid filled, and demonstrates mild mucosal thickening, which is
nonspecific and likely due to underdistension. Vascular structures are within
normal limits, demonstrating mild atherosclerotic calcification.  There is no
free air in the abdomen.

CT PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:  Multiple loops of large and small bowel are
unremarkable.  There is no bowel obstruction.  The urinary bladder, prostate
gland, and rectum are unremarkable.  There is no free fluid in the pelvis.

There is no mesenteric, retroperitoneal or pelvic lymphadenopathy.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  There is no fracture, or worrisome lytic or sclerotic
bony lesion.  Soft tissues are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Small amount of perihepatic ascites.
2.  Unchanged appearance of gallbladder, evaluated with HIDA scan and
gallbladder ultrasound 11 days previously and shown not to represent acute
cholecystitis.
3.  Focal hepatic hyperdense lesion not seen in ___.  In the
right clinical setting, hepatocellular carcinoma must be considered, and
further evaluation is recommended.  This does not have the appearance of
hepatic injury related to prior biopsy.
4.  Scattered diverticula without evidence of acute diverticulitis.

TWO VIEW CHEST.

Comparison to previous study of earlier the same date.

INDICATION:  End-stage renal disease.  New oxygen requirements.

FINDINGS:  Persistent cardiac enlargement, vascular engorgement, and slight
increase in degree of interstitial pulmonary edema.  Persistent small
bilateral pleural effusions.

MPRESSION:  Slight increase in interstitial edema.

Two-view chest, ___, with comparison to previous study of one day
earlier.

INDICATION:  Fever and cough.

FINDINGS:  Interstitial edema has slightly improved with minimal interstitial
abnormalities remaining.  Small right pleural effusion is unchanged.  No areas
of consolidation are identified to suggest the presence of an acute pneumonia.

CT CHEST WITHOUT CONTRAST

REASON FOR EXAM:  ___ man with ESRD on hemodialysis with several
episodes of asymptomatic hypoxia, evaluate for cardiopulmonary process that
would explain hypoxia.

TECHNIQUE:  Chest MDCT was performed without contrast using 5-mm and 1.25-mm
axial slice thickness.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were also obtained.

FINDINGS:  Since ___, central venous line was removed.  Moderate
cardiomegaly slightly increased, although this study is not designed for
accurate measurement of heart size.  Small pericardial effusion is unchanged.
Bilateral pleural effusion cleared.  Mild distension of the esophagus
increased, now fluid filled with an air-fluid level.  Multiple scattered
mediastinal lymph nodes are still not enlarged using CT criteria.  Soft tissue
in the anterior mediastinum is unchanged, could be a conglomerate of lymph
nodes or residual thymus.  Anemia is suggested by relative hypodensity of
intracardiac blood.

Minimal heterogeneous lung attenuation is likely due to airtrapping.  Septal
thickening is minimal, associated with minimal diffuse bronchial wall
thickening, could be due to mild volume overload.  Right lower lobe calcified
granuloma is unchanged.

This study was not tailored for subdiaphragmatic evaluation except to note
small gastrohepatic, peripancreatic and retroperitoneal lymph nodes, not
enlarged using CT criteria and peripheral atherosclerosis of the upper
abdomen.  Liver lesion imaged on previous exam is not depicted on this
noncontrast study.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Moderate cardiomegaly and minimal septal thickening, could be due to mild
volume overload.

2.  Unchanged small pericardial effusion.

3.  Mild esophageal distention with no imaged mass, could be due to reflux in
the appropriate clinical context, would need contrast swallowing examination
to assess .

4.  Unchanged scattered mediastinal lymph nodes and anterior mediastinal soft
tissue, could be small lymph nodes or thymus.

5.  Mild airtrapping.

6.  Possible anemia.
